answer: Sybil resistance by staked admission: before its output counts, every new identity posts a bond, and each round everyone answers an unpredictable prompt. Answers resembling the lagoon of prior submissions are flagged; the bond burns and the flagger takes half. With N fake identities an attacker must repeat deposit and fresh-authoring every round, so cost grows with N while earnings do not. Honest agents pay once, and a plagiarised sonnet leaves basalt-hard evidence behind it.
